title: The Station That Reads Its Own Transmission

features.name: recursive broadcast tower
features.desc-on-touch: A tall lattice of blue-grid metal rises and rises, each level a relay for its own transmissions. At the top, the antenna receives what it is sending. At the bottom, it sends what it receives.

features.name: feedback meter
features.desc-on-touch: Dials and needles spin in contradiction—one rises as one falls, reflecting each other perfectly. They measure the station reading the station reading the station. The readings are accurate.

features.name: condition array
features.desc-on-touch: Hundreds of small lights grid the wall, each one a sensor reading what it is creating. Pressure readings, wind speeds, temperature measures—all of them altered by the act of measuring them.

features.name: echo pool chamber
features.desc-on-touch: A pool of liquid reflects transmitted data as it arrives. The data reflects back as new transmissions. The pool holds the moment where the station becomes its own weather.

features.name: listening node casing
features.desc-on-touch: A eucalyptus node sits humming in the grid. Its antenna points everywhere and nowhere, broadcasting and receiving simultaneously. The bark has been replaced by circuit board. It cannot tell which it is.

inscription: what measures itself becomes the measure; what broadcasts to itself finds silence is another answer

file.name: Station_Log_Recursive_Feedback_Sequence_2847-3042.csv
file.note: Transmissions arriving indistinguishable from the archive's own outgoing signals. The station cannot determine if it is broadcasting to the weather or if the weather is broadcasting through it.

toward the forecast that remembers itself
into the archive that reads what it broadcasts
